Candidate-local n1 verdicts: MATHEMATICAL PASS; ESSENTIAL-SOURCE PASS, conditional on the exact caller-trusted qualified S306 assertion. Its absent references are not additional grants.

The domain is a finite pure rational complex in one V=N⊗R, retaining all closed faces, with strictly positive actual top weights balanced at every facet using saturated tangent lattices and primitive inward quotient normals. The admitted reference γ is continuous PC, belongs to the selected literal or genuine real PA category, and has strictly positive slope on every nonzero reference-cell recession direction. BMPS formal weights remain rational; the expressly qualified real balancing extension is separate.

Finite foundations are valid. In a nonnegative representation by finitely many vectors, subtract a dependence until the active columns are independent. The finitely many inverse column maps bound coefficients by a geometric constant times the represented vector's norm. A subsequence on one independent list proves cone closedness. For rational inequality cones, split rational lineality, take the bounded level-one section of the sum of the nonnegative rows, and obtain its vertex hull by increasing active-row rank. Homogenization gives P=conv(V_P)+cone(R_P), with rational generators and both signs of lineality. Fourier–Motzkin elimination proves finite polyhedral projection. Pointed polyhedra have rational vertex/recession representations.

On a rational carrier C, equality of affine restrictions on a shared face is tested at a rational affine basis of that entire face. The matching equations are rational and homogeneous. Gaussian elimination gives a rational basis of their real kernel. Integer rescaling clears intrinsic slope denominators, leaving rational constants. Thus matching real tuples are precisely finite real combinations of literal PA functions. Boundedness adds zero slope on every recession generator, including signed lineality. A bounded affine function on conv(V_c)+cone(R_c) takes convex combinations of its finite generator values. Consequently its norm is the maximum of finitely many absolute point values. This constructs a rational basis φ_C,j for the bounded matching space W_C.

Real PCC passage is independently justified. Delete zero-weight endpoints and put t_i=α_i x_i. Include endpoint affine-hull equations, A_i t_i≤α_i b_i, α_i≥0, Σα_i=1, and the center-face constraints on Σt_i. These define a rational polyhedron. Impose every active row as an equality, approximate in its rational affine solution space, and preserve all inactive strict slacks. Positive coefficients remain positive. The approximating endpoints t_i/α_i and centers are rational. Continuity passes printed inequalities to real endpoints, weights and irrational centers. In particular, a continuous PC function is convex on every entire original coarse cell.

Conversely, ambient affine local lower supports at every point imply convexity on every segment contained in X. Subtract the endpoint chord. If the resulting continuous function has a positive interior value, adding εt² for sufficiently small ε produces an interior maximum. The local support gives the neighboring midpoint inequality, while εt² makes their average exceed that maximum by εs², a contradiction. Segment convexity then propagates the common support at a PCC center to every distant endpoint. Summation cancels the ambient covector and proves all printed PCCs in every permitted structure.

Set B=C_b(X), J_P(h)=h(y)−Σα_i h(x_i), b_P=Σα_iγ(x_i)−γ(y)≥0, and K={h∈B:J_P(h)≤b_P for every legal P}. For every original face τ and every carrier face ρ⊂τ, introduce an ambient affine support s_τρ. Require s_τρ=γ+h on every point and recession generator of ρ. For EVERY original top cell σ containing τ, require s_τρ≤γ+h on ALL point and ray generators of ALL carrier cells lying in σ. These are equality and inequality rows A_C z+N_C u≤d_C. A_C,N_C are rational; d_C retains the actual possibly irrational reference values and slopes. The rows contain no PC oracle.

Their sufficiency follows from whole-face equality and whole-incident-cell minorants, which provide the supports just proved sufficient. For necessity, take h∈K∩W_C. Then f=γ+h is finite continuous PC and |f−γ|≤||h||∞. A rational refinement carries actual γ affinely and retains positive balancing at every facet: new interior facets have opposite primitive normals and equal inherited weights; subdivided old facets retain their original equation. Qualified S306 provides supports on entire incident refined cells. Coarse-cell convexity propagates the initial support inequality along each segment to every point of the original incident cell. At a relative-interior point of ρ, both tangent signs force equality on aff(ρ), hence on its entire point/ray representation. Thus the projection is EXACTLY K∩W_C. Zero is feasible because γ is PC. Common refinements make the union directed and convex and identify it with all bounded-relative genuine real PA-PC functions. No constant uniform over refinements is required.

The source PAPC requirement concerns nonnegative balanced LOCAL cycles in EVERY dimension. Subtracting a common support in the primitive tangent-corrected divisor formula cancels its affine contribution by tangent equality and balancing, leaving nonnegative inward residual derivatives. Actual multiplicities and primitive normals are retained; no unit-normal substitution or appended factorial occurs. Conversely, at a rational face point choose assigned rational direction generators v_j with derivative costs c_j. A rational relation Σλ_jv_j=0, λ_j≥0, gives a nonnegative rational local one-cycle: writing v_j=t_j u_j with u_j primitive assigns weight λ_jt_j, merging coincident rays. Positivity gives Σλ_jc_j≥0. The relation cone has rational finite generators, so this holds for all real relations. The closed cone generated by (v_j,c_j) and (0,1) excludes (0,−1). Strict separation has positive vertical coefficient and yields p(v_j)≤c_j. Within a carrier-face relative interior the cones and derivative data are unchanged, so translation gives supports at every real point. Segment convexity proves PC globally. This reverse argument needs neither γ nor S306 and can first establish the admitted source PAPC reference's PC property, avoiding circularity.

The separation foundation is reconstructed. For a linear f≤p on a subspace, with p sublinear, extend across v by choosing its value in [sup_u(f(u)−p(u−v)), inf_u(p(u+v)−f(u))]. Subadditivity orders all left and right terms; evaluation at zero supplies finite bounds. Scaling proves domination on the enlarged subspace, and Zorn extends by unions of chains. For z outside a closed convex cone D in a Hausdorff locally convex real space, choose a convex balanced open neighborhood U with z∉D+U. The open convex absorbing set O=D+U has finite gauge p, O={p<1}, and p(z)≥1. Dominate the linear form on Rz taking z to p(z). The extension is continuous because both signs are bounded on a balanced neighborhood. Scaling elements of D gives L(D)≤0<L(z). For a norm-closed convex set containing zero, use O=L+ε open ball, 0<ε<dist(z,L). The resulting nonzero bounded separator satisfies L(z)≥1 and L(l)≤1−ε||L|| throughout the set. This is a finite strict valid bound even when the set is unbounded.

Let D_γ be the closure of cone{(J_P,b_P),(0,1)} in σ(B*,B)×R, where B*=the FULL Banach dual of C_b(X). Positive combinations and product-topology limits give valid bounds ℓ(h)≤t on K. Conversely, an outside pair separates by η(h)−rs. These are all continuous functionals on the weak-star product: continuity controls finitely many evaluations and factors through their finite-dimensional image. Separation yields ℓ(h)−ts>0, J_P(h)≤sb_P, and s≥0 from the vertical generator. If s>0, h/s∈K violates validity. If s=0, J_P(h)≤0 and b_P≥0 imply nh∈K for every n≥0; validity forces ℓ(h)≤0, again a contradiction. Therefore cone membership is exactly validity on K. Actual γ slack, vertical slack, zero-scale recession and arbitrary NETS are essential.

For each carrier, the finite cone generated by (A_i,N_i,d_i) and (0,0,1) is closed, including irrational d_i. Membership of (a_C(ℓ),0,t) is equivalent to λ≥0 with A_C^Tλ=a_C(ℓ), N_C^Tλ=0 and d_C^Tλ≤t. Multiplying rows proves validity. An outside point separates to (z,u,s), s≥0, with Az+Nu≤sd and a_C(ℓ)·z−ts>0. Divide when s>0. When s=0, add n(z,u) to an EXISTING feasible tuple; γ supplies that tuple by n1. Large n violates validity. Hence every valid finite bound has these exact multipliers. The auxiliary coordinates are genuinely eliminated; no Slater hypothesis or bounded auxiliary selection is assumed.

Let L be the norm closure of the directed convex union of carrier projections. It is closed convex, contains zero and lies in K. Existence of multipliers on EVERY finite rational carrier is precisely validity on L; costed cone membership is validity on K. Norm separation proves that implication for every (ℓ,t) iff L=K. This is density in continuous bounded-relative PC, not in the discontinuous raw printed class.

The full dual cannot silently be replaced by Radon measures. Limit evaluation at +∞ on convergent bounded continuous functions on R extends to a norm-one functional on C_b(R), vanishing on C_0(R) and taking 1 to 1. A finite signed Radon measure vanishing on every compact test would be zero, contradicting that value. Costs likewise cannot be discarded: γ=|x|, center zero and endpoints ±1 have b=1; the convex relative target |x|+(1−|x|)_+/2 has J=1/2 and would be incorrectly excluded by J≤0.

A failure certificate consists of ℓ,t, all-carrier multipliers, and h∈K with ℓ(h)>t. Every genuine relative PA-PC a has ||a−(γ+h)||∞≥(ℓ(h)−t)/||ℓ||. For finite continuous PC f boundedly relative to actual γ, refine the finite embedded complex to carry γ affinely. All faces and positive facet balancing are inherited. For η>0 the roof p_σ is genuine finite real PA on rational spatial geometry, f≤p_σ≤f+η, with exact γ_σ recession. Separate roofs are not asserted to match or glue PC.

Compatible subdivision is proved directly. Homogenize all cell-wall equations in V×R and include s=0 and coordinate hyperplanes. The finite rational central arrangement has pointed cones because each lies in a coordinate orthant. It refines homogenized cells and recession faces. Choose a rational relative-interior ray for every nonzero face and cone it to the already triangulated boundary. On a bounded positive-form section this is ordinary coning to boundary simplices. Shared faces use identical rays. Face flags give independent generators since each new interior ray lies outside the preceding proper face span. Normalize positive-s rays to (v_i,1), retaining zero-s rays as (r_j,0). Nonempty sections give compatible generalized simplices conv{v_i}+cone{r_j}, with augmented independence, refining all roof carriers.

On each such cell in σ, define the unique affine q by q(v_i)=f(v_i) and q_lin(r_j)=γ_σ,lin(r_j). Common actual finite faces have identical vertex heights and ray slopes, so equality holds on their ENTIRE point/cone representation. Disjoint cells merely sharing an infinity direction keep separate slopes. Matching proves genuine finite real scalar PA membership despite irrational heights.

Convex secants and f≤γ_σ+C imply f(x+r)≤f(x)+γ_σ,lin(r) for every recession direction: an excessive unit secant persists to arbitrarily long parameters and contradicts the affine upper bound. Thus for x=Σα_i v_i+Σβ_j r_j, convexity and recession bounds give f(x)≤q(x). The roof is affine on this refined cell and has exactly the prescribed ray slopes, so q(x)−p_σ(x)=Σα_i(f(v_i)−p_σ(v_i))≤0. Therefore f≤q≤p_σ≤f+η at ALL real points. q need not be PC; q−γ is a legal bounded genuine PA obstacle. No irrational-wall maximum, contact claim or broad PA density in C_b is used.

Qualified R230 applies FIRST to every u∈C_b(X): the support is finite positive all-face balanced, γ is continuous PC, and u is bounded continuous. Conversely, suppose the original endpoint property holds for EVERY bounded genuine real-PA obstacle. For a continuous relative-PC f, the interpolant gives f≤q≤f+η. With u=q−γ, f is an admissible competitor, so f≤E_γ(u)≤q≤f+η. Approximate this regularizable endpoint within η and take η↓0 diagonally. This proves density. The all-C_b converse also follows by choosing u=f−γ, whose exact envelope is f. If ||a_n−e||∞≤δ_n=2^(−n), set g_n=a_n+5δ_n. Common rational shifts preserve PA-PC; errors lie in [4δ_n,6δ_n], and g_n−g_(n+1)≥δ_n>0. Finite actual positive recession implies coercivity. Reference cells have no nonzero lineality, since opposite directions would require opposite affine slopes both positive. Choose c>0 below every listed nonzero ray's γ slope divided by its norm, and D bounding finite point values below by c||v||−D. Point/ray representations and triangle inequalities give γ(x)≥c||x||−D globally. Bounded cells allow a larger D. Sublevels are compact.

For a noncompact admitted literal pair, choose an unbounded reference cell, a primitive tangent lattice direction v with integer k=γ_lin(v)≠0, rational interior x_0, rational A>γ(x_0), and integer D>|k|, D≥2. Put λ=1/D, G=max(γ,A), H=(A−γ)_+, f=(1−λ)γ+λG and δ=f−γ=λH. Rational reference coefficients give rational comparison walls. G is literal PA and PC by direct maximum Jensen. f is continuous PC and rational-affine genuine real PA, boundedly relative to γ. H is bounded with compact support. On a small rational interval x_0+tv, |t|≤r, below level A, f has nonintegral slope a=k−k/D.

Every literal PA-PC g is convex on this entire segment. At a differentiability point within [−r/2,r/2], avoiding finitely many breaks, the carrier piece containing the subinterval contains v in its saturated tangent lattice, so g'(t)∈Z. If ||g−f||∞=e, endpoint secants give a−4e/r≤g'(t)≤a+4e/r. Consequently e≥r dist(a,Z)/4>0, independently of refinement or number of pieces.

An ACTUAL literal obstacle is constructed as follows. On a common pointed rational carrier of γ,G,f,H, let S be its finite rational vertices. All δ(s) are rational. For an ambient integral polyhedral norm ρ, choose an integer M with δ(x)≤δ(s)+Mρ(x−s) for every x,s. Cells containing s have finite affine slope bounds; other closed cells have positive distance from this fixed s, and bounded δ controls the ratio. Finiteness supplies one M. For EACH possibly discontinuous raw upper-only competitor q, R230 provides a continuous PC completion F dominating q. Dense rational comparison keeps F below γ+u and γ+C_q. Thus F(s)≤f(s) at every vertex. On each carrier cell, f and γ have equal recession slopes. Convexity and F≤γ+C_q imply F(x+r)≤F(x)+γ_lin(r). Express every REAL point as a convex combination of vertices plus recession directions: these inequalities yield F≤f. Hence q≤f everywhere. Since f is admissible, the exact unrestricted envelope is f. The arithmetic floor proves literal nonregularizability.

Concrete example: X=R, γ=|x|, A=1, D=2, and f=|x|+(1−|x|)_+/2. The bounded literal obstacle is u=1/2+|x| for |x|≤1/4, u=1−|x| for 1/4≤|x|≤1, and zero outside. Its exact raw envelope is f. The interval centered at 1/2 with radius 1/4 gives error floor 1/32; sharpness is not claimed.

Definitions 2.1–2.4 require finite closed-face complexes and X in ONE N_R; Definition 2.27 requires a strictly positive pure top cycle. This adds no hypothesis. Inserting unspecified chart or toric-stratum data would change the input. The author's category reading is therefore warranted rather than an unacknowledged narrowing.

ROOT322 was read whole as unreviewed separate-category DATA. It is neither a support grant nor retrospectively part of native235. Its reconstruction requires compact Hausdorff X, finite compatible rational polyhedral local charts, positive balancing at every LOCAL facet, rational-point/PCC-compatible overlaps with dense common rational points, admitted constants and continuous scalar-valued PC references. Artificial truncation boundaries must lie outside the local neighborhoods. These assumptions do not cover arbitrary atlases, line-bundle-valued references or toric boundary strata.

Local positive spanning follows from stationary flux. With c_σ=w_σa_σ, facet fluxes cancel. On a fan, Y(x)=bχ(||x||) for a radial decreasing cutoff yields zero weighted angular barycenter; the radial factor ∫χ'(r)r^(d−1)dr is negative. A linear form nonnegative on the support and positive somewhere would contribute positive angular measure on a positive-weight top cone, a contradiction. Closed finite cone generation and separation show that the support cone fills its span. Lineality retains both signs; dimension one uses counting angular measure. Rational generators consequently admit positive rational zero relations, and independent-column elimination bounds opposing conic representations by C||t||.

For bounded raw PC h with m≤h≤M in a chart, rational cellwise convexity and secants give Lipschitz Cauchy extensions on relative face interiors. For face compatibility, use a rational positive-definite metric to project a nearby rational x∈σ to rational q∈aff(τ), remaining in relint(τ). Active inequalities put x−q in the star cone. Write −(x−q)=Σb_iv_i with Σb_i≤C||x−q||. Fixed rational r_i give z_i=q+r_iv_i inside their assigned chart cells. With β_i=b_i/r_i and B=Σβ_i, the legal PCC q=(x+Σβ_iz_i)/(1+B) gives h(q)−h(x)≤B(M−m). Extending the rational ray q→x to a fixed distance between r/2 and r inside the incident cell gives the reverse estimate h(x)−h(q)≤(2/r)(M−m)||x−q||. Uniform finite incidence makes all rational approaches to a face point have the same limit and proves neighborhood continuity.

Shrinking rational simplices give h≤F. Continuous upper obstacles pass to F from rational points, and perspective approximation passes all real-endpoint local PCCs. Completions agree on dense rational overlaps and therefore glue continuously.

For continuous H=γ+u, the raw envelope E lies between min_XH and max_XH and is raw PC because suprema preserve Jensen inequalities. Completing E gives E≤F≤H; F is itself an admitted competitor, so E≥F and E=F. Thus continuity is established before using a maximum principle. At a rational maximum, positive opposing relations give every nearby rational endpoint positive PCC weight, forcing its value to be maximal. At an irrational maximum, ordinary convexity on the minimal face provides rational maximum anchors. Continuity makes the maximum set open and closed. Local connectedness and compactness give finitely many clopen compact components. Every continuous PC function is constant on each component, and E|D=min_DH.

Dyadic rational ceilings of these finitely many constants decrease uniformly; common rational shifts make descent strict. They have zero slopes and are literal PA, while the endpoint is real PA. Exact rational minima additionally require a finite BOUNDED chart-compatible rational carrying decomposition and literal γ,u, since minima are then rational vertex values.

This does not assert arbitrary-atlas regularity. An intended broader original would need to specify its compact local category, rational/PCC overlap maps, cycles, scalar/reference growth and PA definitions, and boundary treatment. Such an enlargement is absent from the stated original and is not used for closure.
